lines.en: The expression on Yoo Joonghyuk's face slowly changed as he held me by the collar.
In the past, this would have been the moment I plummeted through the air.
But everything was the reverse of what had happened then.
Whoooooosh!
Instead of falling, I soared into the sky.
Yoo Joonghyuk had thrown me with all his strength.
Yoo Joonghyuk watched me as he grew more distant.
An expression as though he was certain I wouldn't die.
I couldn't hear his voice, but I knew what he was saying.
‘Give it a good hit, Kim Dokja.’
Just as I was about to answer, a tentacle flew in and blocked my view.
The attack narrowly missed me, and I landed on the [Eater of Dreams]' true body. Using the strength in my arms, I clung to its body and moved toward the wound.
Tzzzzzz!
A presence that threatened my life just from touching it.
If I were still an incarnation, I might already have fainted or been on the brink of death. And if this thing had finished descending······ I was afraid even to imagine what would have happened.
Crrrraaaack!
I pried the wound open with all my strength and threw myself inside.
[······I'm sorry. This is somewhere I cannot follow you.]
As strength drained from my entire body, I felt Cheok Jungyeong's power gently disperse.
I had expected this, so I wasn't flustered.
Ssssh.
Before long, the wound connecting this place to the outside closed completely.
I floated in the air like someone drifting through space.
The interior of the [Eater of Dreams] was pitch-black darkness.
A space with neither blood nor flesh.
That was only natural, since a god wasn't a living organism.
Something like the sound of a drum came from somewhere.
Then came whispers. The feeling of someone's gaze on me. There was no air, yet breathing wasn't difficult. Perhaps the very way I existed had changed the moment I entered this space.
And a moment later, every sound disappeared.
The incarnations' screams, and the constellations' messages.
What I saw instead were incomprehensible strings of characters and unknown images.
This was the belly of the [Eater of Dreams].
The place where all the stories it had devoured were gathered.
Among them were Stories I could recognize.
They seemed to belong to the ‘Mother of the Founder.’
「It is all my fault. This foolish history has gone on too long······.」
「I have to protect this land from the nebulas. But there is no one left in <Hongik> now. Where have all the creator gods gone?」
「Hwanung······ I miss Hwanung.」
Just then, a Story carrying a small light approached me and shouted.
「What are you? Why did you come here? Run······!」
The light faded with a faint rustle.
I appreciated it, but I had nowhere to run now.
All ‘Outer Gods’ have the foundations of their existence in the distant outer universe.
Half of its true body was connected to the second floor of the [Dark Castle], but its interior was directly connected to the outer universe.
So this place inside its belly was effectively the outer universe to me as well.
In this world of utter emptiness, nothing to feel but the desire to devour.
The [Eater of Dreams] wanted me.
Swoooooosh······!

The letters scattered like mist began to gather all at once and take shape. Eyes and a mouth the size of a house appeared in the empty air. I couldn't actually be certain they were eyes or a mouth, but as a human, I could only think of them that way.
It seemed to be saying something to me, but I couldn't hear its voice clearly.
A moment later, the letters trembled, and its words began to transform into a form I could understand.
【The scent of an interesting story······.】
The moment those two eyes looked at me, I involuntarily caught my breath.
This was the presence of an Outer God that even Narrative-grade constellations feared.
【A being from an inferior scenario······ how······ can you hear my words······?】
[The exclusive skill, ‘Fourth Wall,’ is activating to an extreme degree!]
The [Fourth Wall] had become more active than in any situation so far.
It was enough to make me feel as though a wall was growing over the surface of my skin.
That must have meant this enemy was that dangerous.

If an Outer God that didn't even belong to the ‘Great Old Ones’ was this powerful, I couldn't begin to imagine what would happen if beings like the ‘Fear of Sarnath,’ ‘Horror from the Hills,’ or ‘Master of R’lyeh’ appeared.
I took a deep breath, then slowly opened my mouth.
“Eater of Dreams. O mighty Outer God.”
The [Eater of Dreams]' mouth of letters twitched, as though surprised by my words.
In its eyes, I wouldn't even be an insect. Just a curious toy it could erase whenever it pleased.
Tzz, tzzzz.
Powerful sparks crackled around me, and the surrounding letters began to circle nearby. I sensed something trying to invade me. But the instant it came close, it recoiled as though having a seizure.
The [Eater of Dreams] spoke with a contemplative murmur.
【What······ are you? A being under some special protection?】
It seemed to have tried to invade my mind. Then the [Fourth Wall] must have repelled it.
Without this skill, my very existence really would have been destroyed long ago.
I steadied myself and looked up at the [Eater of Dreams].
As I mentioned earlier, Yoo Joonghyuk had also been devoured by this thing in his 136th round.
But Yoo Joonghyuk hadn't died then.
In other words, what I had to work with now was his 136th round itself.
I spoke slowly enough to avoid putting it on guard.
“I've come to talk with you.”
【Stories! I like stories.】
The god, responding immediately.
Its terrifying greed nearly made every fine hair on my body stand on end.
“Among the Stories you've eaten, there should be someone named ‘Lee Sookyung.’ Please send her back.”
The enormous face tilted as though puzzled.
【But that······ isn't a story?】
“I'll give you a story in return.”
【What story do you mean to give me?】
Without a word, I pointed at myself.
What that meant was all too clear.
I had just staked my own existence on this gamble.
Its enormous eyelids slowly closed and opened.
【Little constellation······.】
“Yes.”
【Are you proposing a bargain with me?】
Just as I was about to say something, shapes appeared in the air.
They were images made from the Stories the [Eater of Dreams] had devoured.
【A bear does not converse with a fish.】
The image that appeared was an enormous bear, reminiscent of the ‘Mother of the Founder.’
The bear looked around with dull eyes, then snatched a fish drifting through the empty universe.
Looking at the bear, the [Eater of Dreams] continued.
【Just as a human does not negotiate with an insect······.】
There was no way a half-fledged constellation from a remote universe, whose Status hadn't even been properly acknowledged, could bargain with a cosmic god.
In a way, that was only natural.
But I shook my head.
“If an insect speaks like a human, thinks like a human, and acts like a human, you would no longer call that being an insect.”
Two enormous eyes made of letters glared at me.
【You······ have no right to bargain with me. I can take what you possess whenever I wish.】
“Then why are you talking to an insect instead of taking it?”

With the sensation of a deep rumble, the bear that had been devouring fish turned to look at me. Its threatening forepaw grew larger, as though it would strike me down at any moment. Looking at the bear, I spoke.
“A bear only knows how to eat fish. It doesn't know how to savor them.”
The bear's forepaw hesitated for an instant.
“It damages their scales with its rough paws, skewers their innards with its filthy claws, then hurriedly fills its own belly. That's all.”
“Just as I'm not an insect, you're not a bear. Isn't that right?”
The letters in the space churned violently, and the [Eater of Dreams]' face became grotesque. Ordinarily, the sight would have been terrifying, but having read the original novel, I knew.
It was smiling.
It found this situation unbearably amusing.

“Every Story's Status is damaged when it is taken by force. If you crush me and take me now, you won't obtain an ‘intact story.’ You will forever lose the chance to eat a story you could have enjoyed in its finest condition.”
Doom··· doom··· doom!
Once again, I heard something like a drum. A sound like the pulse of an enormous beast. The intervals were shorter than before, and it rang out in an ever-faster rhythm.
Doom! Doom! Doom! Doom!
Again, having read the original novel, I knew what this drumming was.
【Now······ I want to eat you.】
This sound was the [Eater of Dreams]' hunger itself.
I swallowed and raised both hands.
“As long as you keep your promise, I'll gladly give myself to you.”
Sssssss.
Letters rose in wisps like smoke and began to form a shape. A moment later, it took on my mother's appearance.
【Is this what you want?】
I nodded.

【This story has some rather interesting aspects, too. It smelled tastier than the shell of the constellation I ate with it, so I was saving it. I very much want to eat you, but it seems a waste to give this up.】
“Do you intend to act like a beast that can't even control its hunger?”
【Does any human take offense at an insect's insult?】
······You fucking bastard.
Maybe it was because its Status was low among Outer Gods, but this thing didn't know a thing about fine dining.
The mouth made of letters formed a cruel smile.
【Our conversation ends here. I will eat you all.】
Whoooooooosh!
The images of the fish the bear had been catching all leaped into the air, then flew toward me, clacking their sharp teeth like piranhas.
There was nowhere to run.
I couldn't even move my legs, and wherever I ran, I'd still be inside its belly anyway.
“Fuck, fine. If you want to eat me, gorge yourself all you like.”
Instead, I spread my arms wide to welcome it.
“But try eating every last bit of me.”
Crrrunch!

Hundreds of fish rushed in and began tearing into my entire body. They tore at my arms, my legs, my waist, and my face. Terrible pain struck, but there was no blood. What flowed out instead were letters. The Stories and histories I had built up were being torn apart by its teeth and beginning to spill out.
【Ohhhhh······! Wh-what is this?】
The god screamed in ecstasy, as though it had tasted a heavenly delicacy.
I felt as though my consciousness was fading and everything in my head was tangling together.
But I held on.
I had to hold on until it devoured ‘that part’ I had in mind.
【Ohhh······ oh?】
And the next moment, something burst out of me like a waterfall.
It had touched something.
Rrrrrrrumble!
[The exclusive skill, ‘Fourth Wall,’ responds to the vibrations pounding against the wall.]
At last, the moment I'd been waiting for had come.
Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh!
Letters poured out as though from an inexhaustible vessel, forming a torrent that flooded its belly. It was a truly staggering quantity of Stories.
【You, you—what in the world are you······!】
The flustered [Eater of Dreams] shouted at me.
But I had no strength to answer.
Simply staying sane amid the Stories bursting out of me was already a struggle.
I watched the sentences passing before my eyes.
「Looking at the approaching mouth of the [Eater of Dreams], Yoo Joonghyuk spoke.」
It was a passage from ‘Ways of Survival.’
「“Fine. If you want to eat me, go ahead and eat all you like.”」
Yoo Joonghyuk's 136th round.
Devoured by the [Eater of Dreams], Yoo Joonghyuk had found himself in the same situation as me.
【Wh-what is this, what in the world is this······!】
In my place, the Yoo Joonghyuk of ‘Ways of Survival’ answered.

「“You will learn. You will experience the emotions I lived through over 136 repeated lives. The loneliness, the sorrow, the rage I felt during that terrible time, all my hatred for this goddamn world—you will learn it all, with nothing added or taken away.”」
【G-graaaaah······!】
「“You lot think humans are less than insects. Then feel it for yourself, starting now.”」
【Wait, hold on······!】

「“The pain that insect experienced. Feel the history an insect could never endure, feel it vividly as that insect felt it. And if you're still confident you can keep eating me, eat all you like and take all you want!”」

The stories poured out in exponentially increasing quantities, filling the [Eater of Dreams]' stomach as though they would make it explode. Both in ‘Ways of Survival’ and before my eyes. The [Eater of Dreams] ate the stories, and in return, it writhed in agony.
Kzzzzzzzt!
Somewhere inside its belly, cracks began to form.
As though mocking the flustered [Eater of Dreams], ‘Ways of Survival’ spoke.
「The [Eater of Dreams], born in the universe and having lived for eighteen thousand years, realized for the first time then.」
【Groooooooooooh······!】
The scene where Yoo Joonghyuk first defeated a ‘god’ in the novel.
A scene I had read over and over until I had practically memorized it.
In place of ‘Ways of Survival,’ I recited the next sentence.
“「That there were stories in this world that must never be eaten.」”

In the original novel, after swallowing Yoo Joonghyuk, the [Eater of Dreams] resonated with the terrible lives he had experienced, writhed in agony, and ultimately perished. It was a catastrophe brought on by excessive overeating.
But that was the story in ‘Ways of Survival.’
This time, the 136th round wasn't all it would be eating.
【Grooooooooooh······!】
The 3rd round, the 4th round, the 5th round······.
「“Do you know what happens when a human lives for thousands of years?”」
The 36th round, the 47th round, the 69th round······.
「“Have you ever given even a little thought to the pain of a life that repeats endlessly?”」
The 141st round, the 143rd round, the 148th round······.
「“This is human suffering, you fucking tentacled bastard.”」
An endless feast of memories.
Cracks began appearing throughout the swollen space.
Having eaten something it should never have eaten, the [Eater of Dreams] went mad and began rampaging in its frenzy.
But it had nowhere to run.
Because this was inside its own belly.
No one can run away from themselves.
【Groooooooooh!】
The rampaging text soon grew beyond the volume it could contain.
Stories it couldn't absorb ran wild, and before long, the overflowing stories swept through the outer universe like waves. Debris from its shattered stomach tumbled about.
[‘Fourth Wall’ slowly opens its eyes.]
[‘Fourth Wall’ searches for prey.]
Startled, the [Eater of Dreams] looked toward me.
[‘Fourth Wall’ smiles at the ‘Eater of Dreams.’]
Now, predator and prey had switched places.
【Gruuuuuuuh······.】
Crunch! Crrrunch!
Having formed an enormous wall of letters, the [Fourth Wall] began swirling and swallowing the [Eater of Dreams]' Stories. No fine dining (美食), only ravenous consumption driven by pure hunger.
The [Eater of Dreams] transformed into countless fish and various symbolic bodies, struggling to escape however it could, but it could never break free of the wall's relentless suction.
Crrrrunch!
Every Story it has eaten over eighteen thousand years is crushed, ground to powder, and sucked into the wall. The letters on the wall radiated a brilliant light.
Horror entered its voice as it read a story it was not permitted to read.
More than half of it had already been eaten, and its thoughts were appearing as letters on the wall.
「Could this be ■■······'s?」
【Ohhhhhhh······.】
「O Great Old Ones! Where are you all!」

At the last moment, it tried to abandon everything and escape, but the [Fourth Wall] was a step faster. Baring its horrifying teeth, the wall devoured every bit of its stomach, then turned the whole thing inside out and swallowed it.
【Ohhh······ O Great Plotter······ ohhhhhhhh.】
With a dazzling light, the wall's open mouth closed.
[‘Fourth Wall’ has finished devouring.]
[You have defeated an Outer God!]
[The <Star Stream> could not find wording befitting your achievement.]
[An achievement of unknown name is added to your fifth Story.]
[Your Status, which was about to be finalized, is undergoing reevaluation.]
Sssss······.
Fragments of the [Eater of Dreams] drifted about, and I remained with a few Stories in the empty void of the outer universe.
Even though the [Eater of Dreams] had died, the space didn't collapse.
I still couldn't return to my original world.
[The gods of the outer universe are greatly alarmed by news that the ‘Eater of Dreams’ has died.]
[The Outer Gods are investigating what occurred in the scenario.]
[Some ‘Great Old Ones’ cast a glance at you.]
Tzzzzzzzt!
A dry heave rose from within me.
Perhaps having my mind torn apart and eaten had left it with a weak stomach.
“Hah, hah······ bleeeeeurgh!!”
It had been a terrible experience.
So this was what Yoo Joonghyuk had endured in his 136th round.
“Bleeeeeurgh!”
After vomiting a few more times, I pushed through the fragments of Stories and set out to find my mother.
Fortunately, her form had been preserved by the [Eater of Dreams]. Her eyes were closed, her face ravaged.
Was she even alive? I couldn't tell.
I checked my mother's pulse and shook her shoulder.
“Please wake up.”
First, I had to get out of here with my mother.
I looked around.
······Why wasn't the space breaking apart?

In the 136th round, too, there had been a scene where the outer universe collapsed the moment Yoo Joonghyuk killed the [Eater of Dreams], returning him to his original world. The outer universe was sustained by the Outer God's power, so when the god died, it should have broken apart as well. But this time, even though the thing had died, its outer universe still remained intact. Why on earth?
[‘Fourth Wall’ looks at you.]
······Could it be?
[‘Fourth Wall’ shakes its head regretfully.]
[‘Fourth Wall’ is still hungry.]
It was hungry, even after eating that many Stories?
[‘Fourth Wall’ begins sucking in the remaining debris.]
Whoooooooo!
Like a running vacuum cleaner, the mouth protruding from the [Fourth Wall] began sucking in everything else around it. The remaining pieces of Stories and dust, and.
“Wait! Wait a second!”
Even my mother, who had been in my arms.
I flew toward the wall as though swimming.
“Hey! Don't eat that!”
But before I could reach the wall, my mother was sucked inside it.
The mouth gaped wide and devoured my mother's head, her arms, her torso.
“Fuck! I told you not to eat her!”
[‘Fourth Wall’ smiles as though satisfied.]
[‘Fourth Wall’ looks at you and smacks its lips.]
There was something I had to ask.
There was something I still hadn't heard.
But that goddamn wall had swallowed my mother.
Where do beings swallowed by the wall go?
I didn't know.
What was certain was that none of the beings the wall had eaten had ever returned.
Neither Simulation from the Theatre Dungeon, nor the reincarnator Nirvana, nor even the [Eater of Dreams] it had just devoured······.
If even an Outer God couldn't survive, was there any chance my mother was alive?
“Spit her out!”
I began striking the [Fourth Wall] with my fists.
The wall kept smacking its lips at me, but showed no particular sign of eating me.
Bam! Baaam!
The wall's surface trembled faintly under my punches. Hitting it, then hitting it again. Even knowing it was foolish, I didn't stop. I couldn't stop.
How long had I been pounding on the wall? A message appeared on it.
「I remember when I first gave that child his name.」
I stared blankly at the sentence.
It was only a moment later that I realized what it meant.
「He wanted to use dok (獨), meaning ‘alone,’ while I wanted to use dok (讀), meaning ‘read.’ Perhaps he and I had been different all along, from that very moment.」
Groaning, I pounded on the wall.
This was never how I had wanted to hear this story.
「I wanted him to become someone who read, rather than someone who was lonely. That people aren't lonely, at least as long as they're reading something. Perhaps that was what I wanted to believe.」
The moment my fists stopped, countless sentences appeared all across the wall.
So many sentences that I could hardly believe one person's lifetime could contain them all.
「“What do you even do at home? Huh? Why do I have to live like this! How long do I have to keep supporting you and the kid!”」
「“Sookyung, shouldn't you put up with it? You have to think of Dokja. Men only act like that for a little while.”」
「“Ma'am, I think you need to pay a little more attention to Dokja.”」
Curses spilled from my mouth as I began striking the wall again.
Some things I remembered, and some I didn't.
But the emotions of that time were vivid.
「It was hard. Back then, things were so hard for me that I couldn't think of anything else. But thinking about it now, it must have been just as hard for the child.」
The suffering my mother had endured in those days.
The violence she should never have suffered as a woman, as a mother, as a human being.
「“Dokja. Stay in here. All right? Until Mommy tells you to, you must never come out.”」
Amid the words mimicking sounds and movements that continued mercilessly across the text, I was experiencing my childhood once again from someone else's viewpoint.
Although these were things I had undoubtedly experienced, they sounded like an entirely unfamiliar story.
So this was what it had been like.
So painful.
So miserable.
But why had I forgotten all of this?
Why had I only ever tried to forget?
All the while, the wall kept speaking.
「I should have taken him and left. Whatever anyone said, I should have taken the child somewhere far away.」
Why didn't you?
Why didn't you just leave long before that?
「Why couldn't I?」
Long records of remorse and regret.
My mother, who had remained silent as my ‘reality’ all my life,
was finally speaking, now that she had become a ‘novel.’
「It happened late in the evening.」
And at last, the story began.
「“Bring me more booze!”」
My father's voice, shouting for more booze. Shoving my mother, hitting her in the stomach. Threatening her.
「“Y-you! Put the knife down and let's talk!”」
Slowly, my memories were returning.
My younger self, hiding in the room, poked his head out in alarm.
Right. That was when my father had been rampaging with a kitchen knife.
「“Dokja! I told you to stay in your room!”」
My mother shouted and ran toward me.
My drunken father was brandishing the knife threateningly.
「You'll die, I'll die. Huh? Shall we all die? We're all fucked anyway if we keep living like this, aren't we? Huh? Let's all die together!」

Then my mother lunged. My father's body crumpled with a thud. The kitchen knife fell to the floor. Liquor spilled, and a bottle rolled. I knew the scene that came next. My mother would pick up the kitchen knife and stab my father. Then she would tell me. That from now on, we should ‘reread’ everything.
「“A-aaaargh!”」
But.
「“Dokja. No! Put that down!”」
What was that?
「“Dokja!”」
My younger self was staring at my father, holding the knife and trembling violently.

My little self, his face crumpled with tears. The sneer on my father's face, his drunkenly swinging fist. My mother taking the blow instead, and my father stepping on a liquor bottle and slipping. And.
A wet plunging sound, and a gush of blood.
「If I had called for emergency help right away, he might have lived.」
It was an utterly staggering coincidence, and
「I was the only one who could save him, and I alone made the choice.」
that coincidence changed our lives.
「So what I told the child was not a lie. I was the one who killed that man.」
My mother took the knife from my unconscious younger self. After taking several deep breaths, she quietly woke me and said:
「“Dokja. From now on, we're going to reread everything.”」
「“Your father did something he deserved to die for. This was self-defense. Understand?”」
「“Whatever happens, you must never forget that you're the victim.”」
My mother's soft, measured words seep into my ears.
「Perhaps that was when so many things were decided.」
My young mother searched for murder case precedents and manipulated the evidence.
She eliminated anything that might implicate me even slightly,
and made this unplanned killing look like a crime she alone had premeditated.
「That someone would have to live as a murderer. And someone else would have to live as a murderer's son.」
Everything after that was just as I remembered.
“······Was this all it was?”
With my hand braced against the wall, I stood with my head bowed for a long time.
······The truth was, I had known.
I'd thought it might be something like this. I'd thought this was the only reason that could explain my mother's actions.
Why she had suddenly written that inexplicable essay.
Why I had to become a murderer's son.
「I often wonder.」
「Could all of it have been just an excuse?」
「There must have been a better way.」
「Whatever happened, I should never have left that child alone.」
「As a mother, I should never have acted that way.」
「In the end, I am merely a mother who ran away.」
And that was the last sentence.
I waited in case there was more, and knocked on the wall again and again.
But no sentence appeared.
Bang!
It couldn't end like this.
I couldn't let it end this way, after hearing this fucking story.
BANG! BAAANG!
“Spit her out! I said spit her out!”
I began pounding the wall like a madman.
“Fuck!”
The [Fourth Wall] licked my fist.
The blood on my fist, my memories, my stories were sucked into the [Fourth Wall] and became a story.
I wasn't crying.
「Kim Dokja was crying.」
The [Fourth Wall] spoke.
「Kim Dokja silently clenched his fist, and.」
Bang!
「Struck the wall, and.」
BANG!
「Struck it again.」
“Fuck!”
「Kim Dokja shuddered. At everything becoming a story. At the fact that all his actions, all his words were becoming a scenario, becoming sentences on the wall.」
“Shut up!”

「Kim Dokja wanted to know. What could he do. What could he do to break this wall? Could this be the price of reading ‘Ways of Survival’? Was even my entire reality turning into a novel because I'd read it? That was when he heard a sound like a page tearing.」
Riiiiip!
「Kim Dokja thought. ······(Hey)······ What's this now?」
Amid the wall's continuing sentences, I saw words that had slipped unnaturally into the text.
Words intruding into the narration like a note scribbled by someone reading the novel.

「Kim Dokja was startled. ······(Get a grip)······ Who's talking to me? ······(This is your skill)······ Who are you? ······(Don't let your own skill eat you)······ What ······(You idiot, pull your hand out! Now!)」
I looked at the wall sucking in my fist.
「······(Deactivate the skill, Kim Dokja)······」
A realization flashed through my mind like lightning.
I didn't know whose words those were.
I didn't even know whether that was possible.
But what I had to do was clear.
“I will deactivate the [Fourth Wall].”
The letters on the wall shook violently, as though an electric current were running through them. With a craaack―for the first time, I felt something that had hovered around me slowly disappearing.
The wall was collapsing.
The next moment, a message rang out.
[The system error caused by an unknown factor is temporarily corrected.]
[Your ‘Attributes Window’ has been restored.]
[Would you like to view your ‘Attributes Window’ now?]
I could see my Attributes Window?
Several things I'd never understood began to make sense.
The reason I hadn't been able to see my Attributes Window all this time. It had been the [Fourth Wall].
The [Fourth Wall] was a skill that protected me from other beings, but also isolated me from myself.
[Viewing the ‘Attributes Window.’]
[The system configuration is still unstable. The display of some skill names and skill levels is restricted.]
And for the first time, my Attributes Window appeared.
<Character Information>
Name : Kim Dokja
Age : 28
Constellation Sponsor (背後星) : None
Modifier (修飾言) : Ugliest King (Temporary)
Exclusive Attributes : Eight Lives (Hero), the Scenario's······.
But before the Attributes Window could fully appear, the screen suddenly collapsed with a bzzzzzt―and more urgent messages appeared.
[Several constellations are approaching your mental barrier.]
In that instant, I realized my mistake.
Perhaps the constellations had been waiting for this opportunity all along.
For the day my information would be revealed to the world.
[Constellations from the nebula <Vedas> are approaching you.]
[Constellations from the nebula <Olympus> are approaching you.]
[Constellations from the nebula <Papyrus> are approaching you.]
The constellations that had tried to reshape my existence to suit their will were forcing my mind open. Then.
[The exclusive skill, ‘Fourth Wall,’ is reactivated regardless of your will!]
Tzzzzzt!
Exclusive Skills : [Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint Lv.?], [Bookmark Lv.?], [Character List Lv.?], [Fourth Wall Lv.?], [■■■■ Lv.?], ■■■■■■■■······.
Overall Evaluation : ······■■You■■■■■■······?
All the information appearing before me was being hidden inside ‘■.’
Information concealing its identity amid fierce sparks, like countless bricks being stacked one upon another.
Tzzzzzt!
[The constellation, ‘Founder of Humanity,’ lets out a groan.]
[The constellation, ‘The One Who Stabbed His Own Eyes,’ retreats, clutching his eyes.]
[The constellation, ‘Scorpion Goddess,’ steps backward, protecting her tail.]
[Some of the constellations that approached you have been struck and are retreating!]
Tzzzzzt!
Countless letters swirling reassuringly.
The [Fourth Wall], throwing off fierce sparks, was protecting me from the constellations. As though it had never defied me just moments earlier, it was radiating a menacing aura toward them.
[‘Fourth Wall’ bares its teeth at the <Star Stream>.]
I stared blankly at the [Fourth Wall].
The last message came from a constellation I knew well.
[The constellation, ‘Secretive Plotter,’ smiles at you.]
A message distinctly different from those of the other constellations.
······Could the Plotter have seen my information in that brief moment?
Even if so, it couldn't have been all of it.
Even I, who had opened the Attributes Window, hadn't managed to see all the information.
The sparks subsided a little, and the wall turned its gaze back to me.
[‘Fourth Wall’ is angry with you.]
I faced the ‘wall.’
For a long time, I'd thought this ‘wall’ was the boundary between fiction and reality.
Because of this ‘wall,’ I'd been able to adapt to the new world and display an unnatural capacity for judgment even in all kinds of horrifying situations.
But if asked what this ‘wall’ was, I still couldn't give a definite answer.
All I knew for certain was that this ‘wall’ had protected me for a long time.
I'd faced danger again and again, but I'd overcome it because this ‘wall’ was there.
Because this wall was there, I'd made it this far.
I placed my hand against the ‘wall,’ which was swelling its letters toward me.
“I'm sorry.”
[‘Fourth Wall’ trembles.]
The feel of the characters curling around my fingers was unfamiliar.
Was this what the [Fourth Wall] felt like?

The characters written on the wall clung to my fingertips like doctor fish. It seemed to be licking me, and it seemed to be biting me. The sensations couldn't be clearly distinguished, so only comparisons that fell short were possible. The [Fourth Wall] was like a puppy soaked by the rain, like an abandoned child, like a disobedient adolescent boy.
The [Fourth Wall] was······.
The [Fourth Wall] was just like me.
Then a sentence appeared on the wall.
「Kim Dok ja is an i dii ot.」
A sentence that looked like a child's tentative attempt after just learning Hangul.
It was neither a narration about me nor a narration about the world.
Those were the [Fourth Wall]'s own words.
I gave a small laugh and stroked the wall.
After displaying indecipherable characters as though confused, the [Fourth Wall] produced another orderly sentence a little later.
「Kim Dokja thought. So the [Fourth Wall] really was a being with a will of its own.」
······Here it went again.

「Then did the [Fourth Wall] write those words in parentheses earlier, too? But the speech was too coherent for that······ Then who wrote those words? If this really is a ‘wall,’ what on earth is inside this ‘wall’······.」
“Stop reading other people's thoughts.”
[‘Fourth Wall’ turns its head away with feigned indifference.]
[‘Fourth Wall’ tells you never to forcibly turn it off again.]
Keeping my hand on the [Fourth Wall], I continued.
“All right. In return, I have a favor to ask.”
[‘Fourth Wall’ looks at you.]
I took a short breath and spoke.
“Give my mother back.”
The wall briefly vibrated, as though gauging whether I meant it.
Then a sentence appeared on the wall.
「Kim Dokja hated his mother.」
“That's right.”

「Kim Dokja had learned what had happened to his mother all this time. He had learned what she had endured, what kind of life she had lived, and what she had kept hidden. But learning these things did not mean he understood all of them.」
“······That's right, too.”

「That is why Kim Dokja still hates his mother. Human emotions are like that. Knowing someone has hidden wounds as deep as mine doesn't magically make all my own wounds heal at once. No such magic exists.」
“I agree.”
「That was why Kim Dokja could not understand himself. Why was he trying to save his mother?」
“I can't explain it.”
“Not everything can be put into sentences.”
I gazed quietly at the wall and spoke once more.
“I don't have much strength left now. So help me out. Please.”
After a long silence, the [Fourth Wall] merely displayed the following sentence.
「Kim Dokja······.」
Could a being that had entered the [Fourth Wall] ever come back out?
I didn't know whether it was possible.
Still, I had to try.
Gurgle.
Then the wall began to move.
Something came gurgling out of the wall's mouth as it vomited.
It was made up of countless letters.
The letters gathered into words, and the words gathered into sentences. The sentences gathered into paragraphs, and the paragraphs gathered again into a single story.
The story soon became a person.
I gathered my mother into my arms as she lay amid the vomited letters.
Then I spoke to the [Fourth Wall].
“Thank you.”
The [Fourth Wall] shuddered, then began to disperse.
「I'm, sleep, y.」
And little by little, the space around me broke apart.
[The constellation, ‘Secretive Plotter,’ drives away the ‘Great Old Ones’ that were spying on you.]
The darkness of the outer cosmos was lifting.
As spacetime shattered, the scenery around me changed into the second floor of the [Dark Castle].
Then the backlogged messages poured out.
[Your Dark Castle ranking is changing.]
[Your current Dark Castle ranking is 2nd.]
[You have fulfilled the main scenario's hidden objective.]
[You have earned the right to challenge the final scenario of the ‘Dark Castle.’]
Two days had passed since the battle on the plain ended.
Before the god that had descended without warning, all mortals had lost the will to fight.
The wanderers' forces and the forces of <Paradise> alike.
In a sense, what had brought them peace was despair more powerful than anything else.

The leaders of the wanderers and <Paradise> recovered the fallen and brought the situation under control. As the needless unrest subsided, the second floor of the [Dark Castle] was gradually stabilizing. One by one, the rankers who would ascend to the next floor were chosen, and the people agreed to entrust the future of the [Dark Castle] to them.
And now.
Most of those rankers were huddled together in front of a small coffin.
“This guy dies like it's his day job.”
Kim Dokja had breathed his last as soon as he returned from defeating the ‘Outer God.’
His companions thought that was only natural, since he had fought such a mighty being. Jung Heewon spoke.
“He'll come back to life tomorrow, right? It took three days last time, too.”
By now, his companions were quite accustomed to Kim Dokja's deaths and didn't seem particularly shocked. Yoo Sangah lightly bit her lip.
“······But did we really have to put him in a coffin?”
“Well, we couldn't just leave a dead person lying in bed······.”
Jung Heewon spoke as though making an excuse.
Each of his companions looked at Kim Dokja's coffin with different feelings.
There was respect in Lee Hyunsung's eyes, guilt in Shin Yoosung's, and conflicted feelings in Yoo Sangah's. And······.
“What brings you here, Master? I thought you'd gone off to find another hidden piece······.”
At Lee Jihye's words, everyone looking at the coffin turned their gaze to the same place.
Yoo Joonghyuk frowned under their collective gaze and answered.
“The only hidden pieces left in the [Dark Castle] are insignificant.”
“But that's no reason to come here······.”
“We need Kim Dokja to advance to the next floor.”
“Hmm······ Haven't you two been awfully close lately? I saw you two days ago, too······.”
As Yoo Joonghyuk's expression grew fiercer, Lee Jihye shut her mouth in alarm.
Jung Heewon gave Lee Jihye a few light taps and chided her.
“Stop teasing Joonghyuk-ssi. It's nice to see them finally getting along. Don't get in the way.”
“······Aw, but still.”
“And you don't need to ask why he's here. It would be the same for anyone.”
At those words, a peculiar solemnity settled over their expressions.
They quietly looked down at Kim Dokja's coffin.
Jung Heewon spoke again.
“Even if they can come back to life, everyone must still be afraid of dying.”
Having several lives didn't mean everyone would use them for others. Shin Yoosung, stroking the coffin's surface at its very front, spoke.
“If it weren't for Dokja-ajusshi, I'd be dead by now.”
Wasn't that true of all of them?
Lee Hyunsung, Jung Heewon, Lee Gilyoung, Lee Jihye.
Every one of them had been saved by Dokja at least once.
Lee Jihye spoke with something like a sigh.
“I wasn't going to say this because it's so cringey······ but if I had two lives, I might have given one to ajusshi.”
“Your affection score is only 6 points, noona. Hyung probably wouldn't take it.”
“You little brat······ It's all the same once you put on the garter belt anyway, you know?”
The companions smiled as they watched Lee Jihye and Lee Gilyoung bicker.

It was hard to believe these were the people who had been crying in despair on a blood-soaked battlefield only two days earlier. Yoo Joonghyuk alone couldn't fit into that scene. He watched them from a little distance away.
His plans had changed considerably with Kim Dokja's arrival.
Scenarios that could have been easy had become difficult, and a simple story had become complicated.
And people who should have died were alive.
Yoo Joonghyuk quietly looked down at his hands.
Perhaps Yoo Joonghyuk himself was among those ‘people who should have died.’
Yoo Joonghyuk found that profoundly strange.
That this scene could have been created by a single person who wasn't even a regressor.
That this round might turn out better than any round he had lived through before.
It left him with deeply conflicted feelings.
“Oh, but that ‘Fate’ thing······ It's over now, right? Dokja-ajusshi died.”
Several companions answered Lee Jihye's question.
“Oh. Right. Now that you mention it.”
“It said he was fated to die at the hands of the person he loves, so hasn't Fate been fulfilled? When you think about it, he died because of his mother······.”
“You're right. Why didn't we think of his mother?”
Their voices rose in animated chatter. From a distance, Yoo Sangah was looking at Yoo Joonghyuk with a conflicted expression. Yoo Joonghyuk met her gaze and thought.
‘[Fate] isn't over.’
Even if they had somehow managed this time thanks to the unexpected factor of Cheok Jungyeong, the nebulas were no pushovers.

There was no way the nebulas hadn't known about Kim Dokja's resurrection attribute, so [Fate] would never end this way. Moreover, this incident must have greatly angered the nebulas at Kim Dokja. They were now likely to intervene in some way to bring about a malicious fulfillment of [Fate].
Above all, the very next scenario, which would begin shortly, was a major hurdle.
So Yoo Joonghyuk, too, had to make a choice now.
He quietly looked up at the sky.
As though searching for something there.
A moment later, a gaze met his from empty space.
[The constellation, ‘???,’ looks at its incarnation.]
The constellation ‘???.’
Even though he was already living his third round of life, Yoo Joonghyuk still didn't even know who his constellation sponsor was.
The being responsible for all these regressions, the being that had inflicted terrible tragedies on him.
Inwardly grinding his teeth, Yoo Joonghyuk took a short breath and spoke.
‘Sponsor. I have something to ask you.’
